scope_verdict: M181 is a correct and useful exact-payload analytic screen. Fixed-pair K4 should be rejected and K8 should advance to implementation screening, but no M181 ratio is physical, complete-FC2, system, or headline evidence.

fixed_pairing_decision.qualification: The all-105 and per-stage selections are posthoc on the same population. They are used only to stress the reject decision, not to create a positive claim.

k8_depth_audit.qualification: The review-only depth screen uses the same 120 payloads and deeper buffers, has no holdout, and is not admitted as a new M181 or headline ratio.

selection_bias_audit.effect_on_fixed_pair_reject: none; independent enumeration of all 105 perfect pairings still loses to D1 K4
selection_bias_audit.effect_on_k8_positive_claim: K8 remains an in-sample architecture scale point only

P1.finding: The 97,607,807-cycle K8 point assumes eight simultaneous bank-unique event lanes, but eight weight-bank responses, eight accumulator lanes, producer/directory bandwidth, and the cross-descriptor source selectors are excluded. The 1.307080x schedule gain over K4 can be erased by area, fmax, SRAM ports, or response stalls.
P1.required_action: Implement the independently depth-screened K8 reservoir, run VCS/SVA and matched Synopsys timing/area, then compose weight response and accumulator service before admitting any physical ratio.

P1.finding: M181 correctly says K8 reuses K4-selected D={2,4,8,8}; it is not an independent K8 depth optimization and all selection is on the same 120 payloads. A review-only sweep found D={2,4,16,32} and 95,410,406 cycles, demonstrating that depth materially changes the result.
P1.required_action: Predeclare feasible depth/storage points, include area/fmax constraints, and confirm on held-out sequences or density strata.

P1.finding: Fixed bank ownership removes the global top-four bank sort, but it does not make the whole frontend wiring-only: each lane still needs cross-descriptor source selection, window storage/control, and same-cycle handoff logic. Hardware simplicity has no RTL or DC evidence in M181.
P1.required_action: Use narrower wording ('fixed bank ownership removes global bank sorting') until RTL/DC establishes selector and control cost.

P2.finding: README says XOR4 is 2.7995% slower than D1. 2.7995% is instead D1's cycle reduction relative to XOR4; XOR4 is 2.8801% slower than D1 when D1 is the denominator.
P2.required_action: Correct the sentence or state the exact ratio 144,146,504 / 148,298,103 = 0.972005.

P2.finding: README reproduction names an absent /tmp/m176_payload.QWZFzA path and does not show extraction of the pinned M51 tar.zst. Per-file SHA checks preserve numeric identity, but the command is not directly runnable after reboot.
P2.required_action: Document archive SHA aa261ebe... and a deterministic extraction or direct-archive command.

P2.finding: M181 evaluates seven XOR perfect matchings, not all 105 fixed perfect matchings. The broad rejection happens to be robust: this review evaluated all 105 and even the best is 2.7807% slower than D1.
P2.required_action: Either narrow the main wording to XOR-fixed pairing or cite/seal an all-105 screen before making the broad fixed-pair rejection.

recommended_m182_gate: Use K8 depths as predeclared implementation points rather than retroactively promoting the review-only 4.444593x ratio.
VCS/SVA must cover zero tokens, partial windows, both buffers closed, release/refill, cross-descriptor selection, all output-block modes, stalls, and malformed directory fail-close.
Matched DC must report area, sequential bits, logic depth, setup/hold, and compare against M180 K4 at identical library/clock assumptions.
Keep 4.344533568x analytic-only until eight-bank weight and accumulator composition are executable.
